newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. to propose 10 pct business tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. to propose 10 pct business tax cut.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson will propose a 10 percent cut in business and corporation taxes, cabinet members said on Tuesday.

The tax cut, which will be announced by Wilson during his State of the State address tonight, would be phased in over two years, the officials said. The tax cut would reduce the state's business and corporation tax rate to 7.96 percent.
"We have got to make sure businesses stay here and come here," Sean Walsh, Wilson's press secretary, said.
Last year, Wilson, a Republican, had proposed a 15 percent across-the-board tax cut. But the state Legislature only approved a five percent business and corporation tax break.

During his State of the State address, Wilson will also propose an overhaul of the state's welfare program, changing it from an entitlement program to a temporary assistance program, Wilson's health and welfare advisers told reporters.
In addition, Wilson will propose the opening of three new trade offices in a bid to boost international commerce with the state, the officials said.
Wilson will present his specific budget plans later this week. The budget proposal will include nearly $1.3 billion to help fund class size reduction, officials said.
